easy.explanation: Proverbs 14:1 says, “Every wise woman buildeth her house.”
easy.q: What does the wise woman build?

answers: He that walketh in his uprightness
easy.explanation: The upright person is described as fearing the LORD.
easy.q: Who fears the LORD?

easy.explanation: A faithful witness will not lie.
easy.q: What will a faithful witness not do?

answers: She plucks it down with her hands
medium.explanation: The foolish woman destroys her house by her own actions.
medium.q: What does the foolish woman do to her house?

medium.explanation: The expression pictures proud and harmful words coming from the foolish.
medium.q: What is a “rod of pride” in the mouth of the foolish?

medium.explanation: Much increase comes by the strength of the ox.
medium.q: Why are oxen useful according to verse 4?

answers: Wisdom builds and preserves, while folly destroys and deceives
Wisdom avoids work, while folly works
Wisdom seeks blame, while folly seeks truth
challenge.explanation: The verses contrast building, integrity, and wisdom with destruction, pride, and deceit.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears between wisdom and folly in these verses?

challenge.explanation: The passage warns that a foolish man may not possess the lips of knowledge.
challenge.q: What can be learned from going away from a foolish man?

challenge.explanation: Truthful and wise speech can preserve people, while false or proud speech causes harm.
challenge.q: What do the faithful witness and wise lips have in common?

paragraphs.title: The Fate of the Wicked, the Path, and Inner Emotion

easy.explanation: The house of the wicked shall be overthrown.
easy.q: What will happen to the house of the wicked?

easy.explanation: A way that seems right may end in the ways of death.
easy.q: What may be the end of a way that seems right?

easy.explanation: A wise man fears and departs from evil.
easy.q: From what does a wise man depart?

answers: The house is overthrown, but the tabernacle flourishes
medium.explanation: The verse contrasts the destruction of the wicked with the flourishing of the upright.
medium.q: What is the contrast between the wicked house and the upright tabernacle?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the final outcome of the way.
medium.q: What does “the end thereof” mean in the verse about the way?

answers: A path that seems right may lead to death
medium.explanation: The verse warns that outward appearance may differ from the final result.
medium.q: Why should a person not rely only on how a path appears?

answers: Outward laughter does not guarantee inward joy
challenge.explanation: The heart may be sorrowful even in laughter, and mirth may end in heaviness.
challenge.q: What does the passage teach about laughter and sorrow?

answers: Both warn against trusting outward appearance alone
challenge.explanation: A path that looks right and laughter that looks joyful may conceal a different outcome.
challenge.q: What do the warnings about the way and laughter have in common?

challenge.explanation: The wise and prudent person recognizes danger and avoids evil rather than acting rashly.
challenge.q: What quality connects the wise man in verse 16 with the prudent person?

paragraphs.title: Anger, Scheming, and the Results of Conduct

easy.explanation: The verse says that he who is soon angry deals foolishly.
easy.q: What does a person who is soon angry do?

easy.explanation: The simple inherit folly.
easy.q: Who inherit folly?

easy.explanation: The passage says that the rich hath many friends.
easy.q: Who has many friends?

answers: A man who makes harmful plans
medium.explanation: The phrase describes someone who devises wicked schemes.
medium.q: What is a man of wicked devices?

medium.explanation: The evil bow before the good.
medium.q: What happens to the evil before the good?

answers: The simple believe every word without careful examination
medium.explanation: The simple believe every word, while the prudent look well to their going.
medium.q: What is the danger of being simple according to these verses?

answers: Quick anger leads to folly, while prudence leads to knowledge
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts angry and foolish conduct with prudent and knowledgeable conduct.
challenge.q: What pattern of cause and effect appears in these verses?

answers: A person’s worth should not depend on wealth
Wealth has no effect on relationships
challenge.explanation: The passage exposes the tendency to hate the poor and favor the rich.
challenge.q: What do the verses teach about treating the poor and the rich?

answers: Those who devise evil err, while those who devise good receive mercy and truth
The evil work while the good rest
challenge.explanation: The verse says that those who devise evil err, but mercy and truth belong to those who devise good.
challenge.q: What is the difference between those who devise evil and those who devise good?

easy.explanation: In all labour there is profit.
easy.q: What brings profit?

easy.explanation: Talk without productive labor tends only to penury.
easy.q: What do the talk of the lips tend to?

easy.explanation: A true witness delivereth souls.
easy.q: What does a true witness do?

medium.explanation: The verse calls the riches of the wise their crown.
medium.q: What is the crown of the wise?

medium.explanation: In this context, profit means useful benefit resulting from labor.
medium.q: What does “profit” mean in the statement about labor?

answers: The foolishness of fools remains folly
medium.explanation: The verse says, “the foolishness of fools is folly,” even when riches are present.
medium.q: Why does wealth not correct the foolish?

answers: Labor produces benefit, while talk alone may lead to poverty
Talk alone is better than work
challenge.explanation: The passage emphasizes the practical value of labor over empty words.
challenge.q: What is the contrast between labor and talk alone?

challenge.explanation: Truthful testimony can protect a person from a false or harmful judgment.
challenge.q: How can a true witness deliver souls?

answers: Wealth may crown the wise but cannot make the foolish wise
challenge.explanation: Riches are described as the wise person’s crown, but folly remains folly in the foolish.
challenge.q: What does the contrast between the wise and the foolish teach about wealth?

paragraphs.title: Fear of God as a Source of Security and Life

easy.explanation: The fear of the LORD is strong confidence.
easy.q: What does the fear of the LORD provide?

easy.explanation: The verse says that the children of the one who fears the LORD shall have a place of refuge.
easy.q: Who shall have a place of refuge?

easy.explanation: The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, to depart from the snares of death.
easy.q: From what does the fountain of life help a person depart?

answers: As strong confidence and a fountain of life
medium.explanation: The two verses describe it as both security and a source of life.
medium.q: How is the fear of the LORD described?

answers: Traps or dangers leading toward death
medium.explanation: The word “snares” refers to traps and dangers.
medium.q: What are the snares of death?

answers: It includes the person and his children
medium.explanation: The passage mentions strong confidence for the person and refuge for his children.
medium.q: What scope of protection appears in these verses?

answers: It directs a person away from deadly dangers
challenge.explanation: The verse connects the fear of the LORD with departing from the snares of death.
challenge.q: Why is the fear of the LORD called a fountain of life, not merely protection?

answers: The fear of the LORD benefits the person’s children
Children have no connection to it
challenge.explanation: The children are specifically promised a place of refuge.
challenge.q: What family continuity appears in these verses?

answers: One emphasizes security, while the other emphasizes life and escape from danger
One describes anger and the other pride
challenge.explanation: The two expressions present different aspects of God-given security and preservation.
challenge.q: What is the difference between strong confidence and a fountain of life?

easy.explanation: The multitude of people is the king’s honour.
easy.q: What gives honor to a king?

easy.explanation: He that is slow to wrath is of great understanding.
easy.q: What does the person who is slow to wrath possess?

easy.explanation: The verse says that he who honoureth his Maker hath mercy on the poor.
easy.q: What does the person who honors God do for the poor?

answers: A sound heart gives life, while envy causes rottenness
medium.explanation: A sound heart is the life of the flesh, but envy is the rottenness of the bones.
medium.q: What is the contrast between a sound heart and envy?

answers: A person who lacks patience and becomes agitated quickly
medium.explanation: The phrase describes someone who reacts hastily and exalts folly.
medium.q: What does “hasty of spirit” describe?

answers: It dishonors the One who made the poor person
The poor person is a king
medium.explanation: The verse teaches that mistreating the poor is an insult to their Maker.
medium.q: Why does oppressing the poor reproach the Maker?

answers: Slowness to wrath is associated with great understanding
challenge.explanation: The passage directly connects being slow to wrath with great understanding.
challenge.q: What connection do the verses make between patience and understanding?

answers: It harms a person inwardly like rottenness in the bones
challenge.explanation: The image of rottenness in the bones describes deep and continuing inner harm.
challenge.q: How can envy affect a person?

answers: Treatment of the poor is also a matter of honoring God
Wealth is more important than mercy
challenge.explanation: Oppressing the poor reproaches their Maker, while honoring Him includes showing mercy to them.
challenge.q: What moral principle is shared by the verses about the poor?

paragraphs.title: The Wicked, the Righteous, and Inner Wisdom

easy.explanation: The wicked is driven away in his wickedness.
easy.q: What happens to the wicked in his wickedness?

easy.explanation: The righteous hath hope in his death.
easy.q: What does the righteous have in death?

answers: In the heart of him that hath understanding
In the house of the wicked
easy.explanation: Wisdom rests in the heart of the understanding person.
easy.q: Where does wisdom rest?

answers: Wisdom is settled within the understanding person
medium.explanation: The word “resteth” emphasizes that wisdom dwells steadily within the heart.
medium.q: What does it mean that wisdom rests in the heart?

answers: The wicked is driven away, but the righteous has hope
medium.explanation: The verse presents opposite outcomes for the wicked and the righteous.
medium.q: What is the contrast between the wicked and the righteous?

answers: It is exposed through what appears among them
medium.explanation: The verse says that what is among fools is made known or exposed.
medium.q: How is what is in the midst of fools made known?

answers: In the understanding person it rests inwardly, while among fools it is exposed outwardly
It is equally hidden in both
In the understanding person it causes noise
challenge.explanation: Wisdom rests in the heart of the discerning, while what is among fools becomes known.
challenge.q: What is the contrast between wisdom in the understanding person and among fools?

answers: The righteous retain confidence even in death
Death is a reward for the wicked
challenge.explanation: The verse presents hope as belonging to the righteous even at death.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the righteous having hope in death?

answers: A person’s inner character is revealed through conduct and outcome
Character has no relation to outcome
challenge.explanation: The wicked are driven away because of wickedness, while wisdom is shown in the understanding heart.
challenge.q: How are the verses about the wicked and wisdom connected?

easy.explanation: Righteousness exalteth a nation.
easy.q: What exalts a nation?

easy.explanation: The king’s favour is toward a wise servant.
easy.q: Toward whom is the king’s favour directed?

easy.explanation: The king’s wrath is against him that causeth shame.
easy.q: What does the king show toward the one who causes shame?

answers: Righteousness exalts a nation, while sin is a reproach
Both righteousness and sin are condemned equally
medium.explanation: The verse gives righteousness a positive result and sin a shameful one.
medium.q: What is the contrast in verse 34?

answers: A servant who is discerning and useful
medium.explanation: A wise servant acts with understanding and performs his duties well.
medium.q: What is a wise servant?

answers: Because that servant fails and brings disgrace
medium.explanation: The verse contrasts the king’s favor toward a wise servant with his wrath toward one who causes shame.
medium.q: Why does the king respond with wrath to one who causes shame?

answers: A leader values intelligent and useful service
challenge.explanation: The king’s favor is directed toward a servant who serves wisely.
challenge.q: What does the king’s response to the wise servant teach about leadership?

answers: Righteousness can elevate a nation, while sin brings reproach
Sin is always better than righteousness
challenge.explanation: The verse clearly contrasts national honor through righteousness with disgrace through sin.
challenge.q: How do the verses distinguish righteousness from sin?

answers: Wise actions bring favor, while careless actions bring shame and wrath
Status determines everything regardless of conduct
challenge.explanation: The servant’s treatment depends on whether he serves wisely or causes shame.
challenge.q: What is the connection between personal responsibility and status in these verses?
